transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Yeah, um… thanks. I guess I’m here because there’s been this situation at work that I haven’t really been able to let go of. I’m a music director and composer, and after a commission I did, it started to feel like a few people in the ensemble were… not openly attacking me, exactly, but sort of quietly working against the piece and my role.

Like schedule changes, where people sat, small comments in rehearsals—things like that. And I know that probably sounds a little hard to explain, because they’ll show me emails or notes that are supposed to account for it, but I still feel pretty certain there’s more going on underneath. I’m not trying to be difficult or dramatic. I just haven’t been able to shake it, and it’s been almost two years now, so I thought maybe it would be good to talk to someone.

Outside of this situation at work, have you generally had a long-standing pattern of feeling suspicious or distrustful of people—like in past jobs, friendships, or relationships—or is this kind of intense mistrust something new that's really specific to this one situation?

I don’t think it’s been a lifelong thing, no. I mean, I’ve had normal doubts about people like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’m usually suspicious in friendships or every job.

This feels… pretty specific to the commission and the ensemble afterward. That’s where I keep getting stuck. It’s been almost two years, and I know people have explanations for the schedule changes or seating decisions or little rehearsal comments—emails and notes and all that—but I still can’t shake the feeling, really the certainty, that a few of them were quietly trying to undermine the piece and my role. I know that may sound a bit much, but that’s honestly how it’s felt.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't seem to notice, during this period?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m a musician, so I’m probably more tuned into sounds than some people, but not in the sense of hearing voices that aren’t there or seeing things other people don’t see.

It’s more about how I interpret what’s happening around the situation, if that makes sense. I’m not trying to make it sound stranger than it is.
Outside of this specific concern about the ensemble and the piece, how have things been going for you—are you still able to work, socialize, and manage daily life without major difficulty?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like everything is falling apart, because it really isn’t. I’m still getting my work done, meeting deadlines, composing, that kind of thing.

I run most mornings, which helps keep me steady, and at home things with my wife are basically okay—steady, I’d say. So outside of this… specific issue with the ensemble, I’m functioning pretty normally, I think.
